issues.description: The problem specification (UML and text) declares checkOrderReady() with a void return type, but the provided solution implements checkOrderReady() as public boolean checkOrderReady(). This mismatch between the documented signature and the solution implementation can confuse students about the expected method contract and return value, and may cause mismatches with tests or the intended API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the declaration consistent. Either update the solution to implement checkOrderReady() with a void return type (removing the boolean return value and any returned flag) to match the problem statement, or update the problem statement/UML to indicate that checkOrderReady() returns a boolean (and document what the boolean means). Preferably change the solution signature to public void checkOrderReady() so it matches the UML and textual description.
